meta.title_plain: How old balls and a tough uncle built the King of Clay
meta.teaser: Bad courts, old balls and Uncle Toni turned Rafa into a 14-time French Open champ.

page.title: How old balls and a tough uncle built the King of Clay
page.sub: The story of Rafael Nadal and his coach, Uncle Toni
page.bigIdea: Rafael Nadal's uncle Toni trained him on purpose in hard conditions. Those tough practices helped Rafa win a record 14 French Open titles.

cards.title: First shots with Uncle Toni
cards.front: Rafa was born in 1986 on the island of Mallorca, Spain.
cards.back: His uncle Toni coached at the local tennis club in Manacor. Rafa hit his first shots with him at age 3. Football was his first love, though.
cards.tryit: Ask a family member who taught them their favourite sport or hobby. Write their answer down.

cards.title: Bad balls on bad courts
cards.front: Toni often made Rafa train with worn-out balls on poor courts. Why?
cards.back: Toni wanted him to stop blaming equipment. Win or lose, it was up to the player. He also stretched 90-minute sessions longer, without warning, to build stamina.
cards.tryit: Play 10 minutes with your oldest, flattest ball. Notice every time you want to blame it, then just play on.

cards.title: The lefty legend
cards.front: Rafa eats with his right hand. So why does he play tennis left-handed?
cards.back: Until about age 10, he hit forehands with two hands. When he switched to one hand, he chose his stronger left. Toni says the 'forced lefty' story is a legend.
cards.tryit: Hit 20 soft forehands with your other hand. Notice which parts feel hardest.

cards.title: Staying home to train
cards.front: At 14, Spain's tennis federation asked Rafa to move to Barcelona.
cards.back: His family said no, partly so school wouldn't suffer. Toni believed you could become great from home. Rafa turned pro at 14 anyway.
cards.tryit: List three places near your home where you could practise tennis for free.

cards.title: The King of Clay
cards.front: From 2005 to 2022, Rafa won the French Open 14 times.
cards.back: That's a record. Ten of those came with Toni as coach. Rafa also won 22 Grand Slams and once won 81 clay matches in a row. He retired in 2024.
cards.tryit: Watch a Nadal clay highlight. Count how many times he slides into a shot.

words.d: A tennis court made of crushed brick. Balls bounce high and slower.
The Grand Slam played on clay in Paris every spring.
The energy to keep going hard for a long time.
Forward spin that makes the ball dip down, then kick up high.
To start playing a sport as your job, for prize money.

quiz.q: Why did Toni make Rafa train with old balls on bad courts?
opts: To save money on new balls
So Rafa would stop blaming equipment
Because the club had no good courts
quiz.hint: Think about what Toni said decides who wins or loses.
quiz.why: Toni wanted Rafa to learn that the player, not the equipment, is responsible for the result.

quiz.q: How did Rafa end up playing left-handed?
opts: He picked his stronger left hand when he stopped hitting two-handed
Toni forced him to switch on day one
He hurt his right arm as a kid
quiz.hint: Card 3 says the famous story is a legend. What really happened around age 10?
quiz.why: When he moved to a one-handed forehand, he used his left, which felt stronger.

quiz.q: How many French Open titles did Rafa win in total?
quiz.hint: It's more than he won with Toni, but less than his total Grand Slams.
quiz.why: Rafa won 14 French Opens, a record, out of his 22 Grand Slam titles.

quiz.q: What did Rafa's family decide when he was asked to move to Barcelona at 14?
quiz.hint: Remember what Toni believed about becoming great.
quiz.why: They stayed home, partly for school, and because Toni believed you could become great from home.

page.think: Toni made practice harder on purpose so matches felt easier. What is one way you could make your own tennis practice a little tougher this week?
tries: Play one practice game to 20 points without complaining about the ball, court or wind once
Do 15 minutes of footwork drills, then add 5 surprise minutes like Uncle Toni would
Watch a Nadal French Open highlight and notice how high his topspin forehand bounces
Tell Dad one idea from this report
